## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the integration loop can approach the streaming ceiling on low-death workloads, with a simple render loop sufficing.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/particle AoS layout offers 32 hot bytes in loop 1 (47%) and 28 in loop 2 (41%); the rest is dead filler. No intermediate storage keeps the death verdict in registers. The approach bets on auto-vectorizing LP1's stride-68 integration while leaving LP2 simple. With 47% hot bytes, perfect streaming would waste half each line, but the working set fits L2 through N≈7700 and L3 through N≈246723, so cache pressure is secondary to codegen quality.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p rises from 21.0 (L1d, N=320) to 23.5 (L2, N=7700) — 12% across the L1d→L2 spill at N≈481, no sharp knee. The L2→L3 transition at N≈7710 is invisible: cost holds ~23–24 ns/p through L3. The L3→DRAM spill at N≈250000 adds only ~1 ns/p. At q=0.5 the curve is flatter (32.0–32.9 across all N) — respawn masks cache effects. The dense grid resolves no knee; backend stalls dominate at every level.

## Bandwidth
Achieved 2.69–3.23 GB/s vs the 12.69 ceiling — 21–25%. The memory floor is 5.359 ns/p; the algo runs at 21–33 ns/p, 4–6x above floor — backend-stall-bound (58–66%), not bandwidth-bound. vs baseline: 0.93–0.99x — at most 7% faster than naive scalar. vs winner: 1.7–3.4x slower, widest at q=0.01/L3 (3.4x at N=160000) and narrowest at q=0.5/DRAM (1.7x at N=370000). The winner (LP2-opt) pulls furthest ahead at low q; at q=0.5 both converge.

## Assembly
Loop 1 shows partial vectorization: `vmovups` loads position, `vmulps`/`vaddps`/`vbroadcastss` integrate, but the death check is scalar (`vucomiss` + `jae`) and respawn is a branchy call — 14 cond-branches, 103 insns/iter. Loop 2 is entirely scalar: 21 cond-branches, 12 `cmovae`, 16 byte-granular stores via `movzx`/add/`cmp`/`cmovae`/`mov BYTE PTR` — no wide-store coalescence. Only 16 of 345 instructions (4.6%) are vector-suffixed, confined to integration math. The 64% backend-stall rate aligns with scalar byte-scatter and branchy respawn capping bandwidth at 25% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.93–0.99x of naive baseline (at most 7% faster) and 1.7–3.4x slower than the winner at every point. LP1's auto-vectorized integration (`vmulps`/`vaddps`) cannot compensate for the branchy respawn (14 cond-branches/iter) and LP2's scalar byte-granular scatter (16 byte stores/iter). At 21–25% of ceiling and 4–6x above the memory floor, the algo is backend-stall-bound (64%) — the 47% hot fraction is irrelevant when the pipeline stalls on branches and byte stores. The winner's 3.4x advantage at q=0.01 confirms LP2 is the bottleneck.
